short: The quantized audio memory (M02) is a standard memory-recall design; its gains repeat over a no-memory baseline, but the LRS3 state-of-the-art claim and the edge over distillation do not hold.
position: The paper [@yeo2024akvsr] changes training-only supervision (M02): HuBERT features are quantized into a 200-slot memory recalled from video, so lip-reader training needs no audio. Recalling an audio memory from video is the same group's earlier design [@kim2021multimodality; @kim2022distinguishing], so the verdict is standard. Its gain over the no-memory AV-HuBERT baseline repeats across LRS3, LRS2, two model sizes and a second backbone. Its edge over distillation is 2.0 points from one LRS3 run, and the memory carries transcripts of 656 h, 22 times the labels of the 30 h comparators (inference). The abstract's unqualified LRS3 state-of-the-art claim fails against a cited work: SynthVSR Large reaches 18.2% without a language model [@liu2023synthvsr] [concurrent], 5.4 points below the paper's 23.6% (inference), though with more training data and an unstated language-model condition.
